senses.gloss: written; it is written, v. כְּתַב I.—[Targ. II Esth. VII, 10 כְּתִיבֵי some ed., read כִּתְבֵי, v. כְּתַב II].
(Massorah) כְּתִיב K’thib, the traditional spelling of Biblical words, opp. to קרי, K’ri, the Massoretic instruction for reading, e.g.
units: <cite ref="Genesis 8:17">Gen. VIII, 17</cite>: K’thib (<cite ref="E00264"><he>הוֹצֵא</he></cite>) <cite ref="E00264"><he>הוצא</he></cite>, K’ri <he>הַיְצֵא</he>; v.
<cite ref="Tractate Soferim 6:5">Treat. Sof’rim VI, 5</cite>; <cite ref="Tractate Soferim 7:4">VII, 4</cite>.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 24b:9">Ab. Zar. 24ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="I Samuel 7:9">I Sam. VII, 9</cite>) <he>ויעלה כ׳</he> the K’thib allows the reading <he>וַיַּעֲלֶהָ</he> (with feminine suffix).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 20a:9">Snh. 20ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="K01095"><he>כָּרָה</he></cite>; a. v. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="K01343"><he>כְּתִיבָן</he></cite>.

Ned. 37ᵇ קריין ולא כ׳ וכ׳ ולא קריין וכ׳ the rules about reading words not written (omitted in the text) and such as are written but not read (marked as superfluous) are a Mosaic (ancient, traditional) halakhah (v. הֲלָכָה).
<cite ref="Nedarim 37b:9">Ib.</cite> <he>הלין קדיין ולא כְתִבָן</he> those (quoted) are those read but not written; <he>וכְתִבָן ולא קריין וכ׳</he> and those written but not read are &c.; v.
